title:
The Last Light
on Marlow Street
description: Rain, a taped-off alley, and one witness who saw nothing, until the streetlight started to flicker.

lines.text: It was raining on Marlow Street, the kind of rain that hides footsteps.
Detective Nia stood behind the yellow tape, watching the alley breathe red and blue.
A man had been found at the far end, beside the old brick wall.
No weapon. No wallet. Only one witness, a girl who swore she had seen nothing.
But the streetlight above the alley had been flickering all night.
Nia noticed it never flickered at random.
It went dark for three seconds, then flashed twice.
Over and over, like someone sending a message.
She followed the pattern to the lamp post and found a small brass key taped beneath it.
The key fit a door that had been bricked over for twenty years.
Behind the bricks was a cupboard, and inside it a single photograph.
It showed the witness, much younger, standing beside the missing man.
The girl had not seen nothing. She had seen everything, and she had been waiting for someone to ask the right question.
